in_text_mentions: [54]. However, in BD sudden hilar enlargement or intraparenchymal round opacities on the chest radiograph or chest CT scan can present pulmonary artery aneurysm [8, 14]. PAAs may be single (Figures 2–4) or multiple unilateral or bilateral (Figure 5). These lesions may be occluded totally or partially by thrombus (Figures 2, 4, 5). Thrombosed aneurysms cause ischemia or infarction in pulmonary parenchyma [8, 20]. In BD hemoptysis can also be misdiagnosed as pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) and this condition could be mistakenly attributed to PTE and inappropriate anticoagulation may prove fatal

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Coronal CT of a 25-year-old man with known Behçet disease directly demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary artery aneurysms, a characteristic pulmonary vascular manifestation, with caption-described mural thrombi. [raw subtype: pulmonary vascular involvement] b: Axial CT directly shows a large right pulmonary artery aneurysm with partial thrombus and surrounding hemorrhage in a patient with known Behçet disease. [raw subtype: pulmonary vascular involvement] c: The lung-window CT demonstrates multiple caption-described subpleural nodular infiltrates in a patient with known Behçet disease and concurrent pulmonary artery aneurysms. This is supported as pulmonary parenchymal involvement, although the provided vocabulary has no matching finding key. [raw subtype: pulmonary parenchymal involvement]

panels.figure_caption: 25-year-old man with multiple pulmonary artery aneurysms who had hemoptysis and chest pain with known BD. (a) Coronal maximum-intensity projection CT (curved multiplanar reconstruction) image showing multiple bilateral pulmonary artery aneurysms and mural thrombi (arrows). (b) Large right pulmonary artery aneurysm (long arrow) is partially lined by thrombus and densely opacified on a volumetric high-resolution CT. Lung window scan at the level (Figure 5(a)) shows the right pulmonary artery aneurysm with circumferential ground glass opacification because of surrounding haemorrhage (arrow): this finding was attributed to intraparenchymal haemorrhage. (c) Chest CT scans (lung window) obtained at different levels demonstrate multiple subpleural nodular infiltrations in the periphery of the right and left lung (arrows).
